title: Customs Amendment (Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement Implementation) Bill 2014
short_title: Customs Amendment (Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement Implementation) Bill 2014

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would change customs law so that goods from Japan can enter Australia at lower duty rates under a trade deal.
It would set rules to decide which products count as made in Japan, based on where they were produced.
The new system would start on the later of the day the bill becomes law or the day the trade deal takes effect for Australia.
changes: Creates rules for determining whether imported goods are Japanese-origin goods.
Allows goods that meet the origin rules to enter Australia at preferential customs duty rates.
Imposes requirements on Australian exporters and producers who claim preferential duty for goods sent to Japan.
summary.affected: Importers and exporters of goods between Australia and Japan, and producers of such goods.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Robb
speeches.brief: Moved the second reading of the Customs Amendment (Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement Implementation) Bill 2014, said more than 97 per cent of Australia's exports to Japan would receive preferential access or enter duty-free once fully implemented, and noted the agreement was signed on 8 July 2014 by Prime Minister Tony Abbott and Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Robb
speeches.brief: Moved the second reading of the Customs Tariff Amendment (Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement Implementation) Bill 2014, which phases preferential tariff rates on Japanese-originating goods to zero by 2021, and creates a new schedule setting excise-equivalent duties on certain alcohol, tobacco and petroleum products.

speeches.speaker: Tanya Plibersek
speeches.brief: Argued that Labor supports the Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement bills but moved a second reading amendment opposing investor-state dispute settlement provisions, criticised the exemption from labour market testing for 457 visa contractual service providers from Japan, and cited industry criticism from groups such as the National Farmers Federation.

speeches.speaker: Eric Hutchinson
speeches.brief: Welcomed the Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement as historic for exporters, arguing it delivers major gains for Tasmanian beef, dairy and cheese producers, noting more than 97 per cent of Australian exports to Japan will get preferential or duty free access, and crediting Minister Robb's negotiation.

speeches.speaker: Jim Chalmers
speeches.brief: Argued that Labor supports the Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement despite some reservations, and paid tribute to the DFAT and Treasury officials and former trade minister Craig Emerson who worked on the agreement over several years.

speeches.speaker: Matt Thistlethwaite
speeches.brief: Argued that Labor supports the Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement bills despite concerns that reduced labour market testing for Japanese workers under 457 visas will cost Australian jobs, noting Australian exports to Japan doubled from $24 billion in 2001 to $50 billion in 2011.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: Supported the Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement, arguing that free trade increases wealth, jobs and living standards, expands export opportunities, supports productivity and lowers consumer prices, including through duty-free Japanese car imports.

speeches.speaker: Rowan Ramsey
speeches.brief: Supported the Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement, arguing it would improve access for Australian agricultural exports, including beef, grain and seafood, while citing reduced tariffs, duty-free barley and new opportunities for regional producers.

speeches.speaker: David Gillespie
speeches.brief: Supported the two bills implementing the Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement, arguing that lower tariffs would improve export competitiveness, farm-gate prices and regional employment, and citing opportunities for beef, dairy, wine, timber and macadamia producers.

speeches.speaker: Wyatt Roy
speeches.brief: Supported the Customs Amendment (Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement Implementation) Bill 2014 and related bill, arguing that free trade agreements with Korea, Japan and China will expand opportunities for exporters, consumers and jobs; highlighted Japanese market advantages for beef, dairy, horticulture and nuts, and Chinese access for Australian services.

speeches.speaker: Nickolas Varvaris
speeches.brief: Supported the Customs Amendment (Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement Implementation) Bill 2014, reporting that the agreement improves access for Australian goods, services and investment; noted more than 97 per cent of exports will receive preferential or duty-free access and cited 2013 two-way trade of $70.8 billion and a $28.3 billion surplus.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Robb
speeches.brief: Concluded debate on the Customs Tariff Amendment (Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement Implementation) Bill 2014, explaining that it implements Australia's tariff commitments under the Japan-Australia agreement; reported its effects on agriculture, resources and services, including a tariff-free quota of 20,000 tonnes for cheese and a 10 per cent initial reduction for frozen beef.
